Article Title: Lausanne Diamond League: Neeraj Chopra finishes second by 9cm as Sri Lanka’s Pathirage seals third straight win
Article Text:
Neeraj Chopra, of India, competes in the javelin during the World Athletics Diamond League athletics meeting in Lausanne, Switzerland, Friday, August 21, 2026. (Laurent Gillieron/Keystone via AP)

Pathirage completes another victory over Chopra

How the competition unfolded

Strong showing from Anderson Peters

Men's javelin final standings

Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage (Sri Lanka) — 88.14m Neeraj Chopra (India) — 88.05m Anderson Peters (Grenada) — 86.69m Keshorn Walcott (Trinidad and Tobago) — 83.71m Marc Anthony Minichello (USA) — 80.06m Curtis Thompson (USA) — 78.13m Jakub Vadlejch (Czech Republic) — 77.32m Artur Felfner (Ukraine) — 74.84m Simon Wieland (Switzerland) — 73.23m

Important points gained in the race for the Diamond League Final

Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage edged out Neeraj Chopra by just nine centimetres in Lausanne, securing his third victory over the Indian star this season and tightening his grip on one of the sport's most compelling emerging rivalries.For a brief moment on Friday night, it looked as though Chopra had finally found a way past the man who had beaten him in Doha and again at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The Indian moved into the lead with a huge second-round throw and produced his trademark roar in celebration.But Pathirage had another answer.The Sri Lankan responded with an 88.14m effort in the third round and held on through the remainder of the competition to claim victory at the Lausanne Diamond League. Chopra finished second with 88.05m, while Grenada's Anderson Peters took third place with a season-best 86.69m.The margin between first and second was just nine centimetres.The result continues a remarkable season for Pathirage, who has now defeated Chopra in all three of their meetings in 2026.Their first clash came at the Doha Diamond League in June, where Pathirage threw 88.68m to finish ahead of Chopra. The Sri Lankan then claimed Commonwealth Games gold in Glasgow, with Chopra taking silver.Lausanne presented Chopra with another opportunity to reverse that trend, and for much of the evening he remained firmly in contention.Instead, Pathirage once again found a way to stay in front when it mattered most.Chopra opened his night with a throw of 83.54m, immediately placing himself among the contenders but still behind Pathirage after the opening round.The competition changed dramatically in the second round.Launching his javelin beyond the 88-metre mark, Chopra produced 88.05m, surging into first place and briefly taking control of the event. The reaction was immediate, with the Indian celebrating what appeared to be a potentially winning throw.That lead, however, lasted only one round.Pathirage responded in the third attempt with 88.14m, moving back into first place and reclaiming control of the competition. Chopra answered with 83.72m in his third throw but could not improve on his second-round mark.The pressure increased as the competition moved into its closing stages.Chopra recorded a foul in the fourth round, reducing his opportunities to regain the lead. In the fifth round, he elected to pass, while Pathirage fouled, leaving the standings unchanged heading into the final attempts.Everything therefore came down to the sixth and final round.Neeraj needed one last improvement to overtake Pathirage, but his final throw travelled only a little over 82 metres, leaving the Sri Lankan free to celebrate another Diamond League victory.While the battle for victory centred on Chopra and Pathirage, Anderson Peters quietly produced one of his best performances of the season.The Grenadian finished third with 86.69m, a season-best effort that kept him comfortably inside the top three throughout the evening.Former Olympic champion Keshorn Walcott placed fourth with 83.71m, while Marc Anthony Minichello rounded out the top five with 80.06m.Although Chopra narrowly missed out on victory, the result could still prove significant for his Diamond League campaign.The Lausanne meeting carried extra importance because Chopra entered the event seventh in the season standings with five points and had not yet secured qualification for the Diamond League Final.Only the top six javelin throwers automatically qualify for the season-ending final, while any additional places depend on wildcard selections.His runner-up finish in Lausanne therefore delivers a valuable points boost ahead of the final qualifying event in Zurich, keeping him firmly in the race for a place at the Diamond League Final.The victory belonged to Pathirage once again, but Chopra leaves Switzerland with another throw beyond 88 metres and a stronger position in the qualification battle. The rivalry between the two has now produced three meetings this season, and all three have gone the Sri Lankan's way. The gap this time was the smallest yet — just nine centimetres.
Article Summary: Sri lanka's rumesh tharanga pathirage edged out neeraj chopra by just nine centimetres in lausanne, switzerland. It is his third victory over the indian star this season and tightening his grip on one of the sport's most compelling emerging rivalries. Chopra finished second, while grenada's anderson peters took third place.

Article Title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader Trinity Miles leaves fans intrigued after revealing the unconventional meal she enjoys during her demanding routine

A Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader has given fans an unexpected glimpse into what she likes to eat away from the spotlight. Trinity Miles recently shared a simple food combination that sounds unusual until she explained the idea behind it. Her bowl brings together turkey, zucchini, sweet potato, cottage cheese, mustard and ketchup, creating a meal she says captures the familiar taste of one of America’s favorite foods.At first glance, Miles’ bowl does not look anything like a traditional burger. There is no bun, no melted cheese and no familiar stack of toppings. Instead, the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader combines several ingredients in a way that fits into her demanding routine.Her explanation was remarkably simple.“It tastes like a burger,” Miles said in a Dailymotion video.That short comment makes the unusual combination easier to understand. The turkey provides the main savory element, while mustard and ketchup bring the flavors commonly associated with a classic burger. Sweet potato adds another layer to the meal, while zucchini and cottage cheese round out the bowl.For someone with an intense schedule, the appeal may be less about making a picture-perfect meal and more about finding food that works around a packed day.Miles has previously offered insight into just how physically demanding life as a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader can be. In a July 16 interview with Garden & Gun, she said her fitness tracker can record between 20,000 and 25,000 steps on a game day. That can translate to roughly eight to 12 miles of movement.Those numbers put her food choice into perspective. A game day involves far more than the minutes spent performing in front of thousands of Cowboys fans. Rehearsals, appearances and other commitments can keep cheerleaders moving for hours.Miles’ food revelation also offers a small window into the routine behind one of the most recognizable names in professional sports entertainment.The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are known for their demanding dance work, athletic performances and highly visible appearances. Their schedule stretches beyond game days, with rehearsals, community events and seasonal performances requiring consistent preparation.That workload helps explain why individual cheerleaders may develop their own practical approaches to meals. Miles’ burger-inspired bowl is a good example. Rather than recreating a burger exactly, she has taken flavors she enjoys and placed them into a different format.It is also a reminder that the polished performances fans see at AT&T Stadium represent only one part of the job. Preparation begins long before the music starts and continues after the final routine ends.The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have built a legacy that reaches far beyond football. The organization says the squad has performed for more than 90,000 fans at Cowboys home games and has taken part in numerous community and military-related appearances over the years.For Miles, being part of that tradition means managing a demanding lifestyle while maintaining the energy required for performance. Her unusual meal may have caught attention because it sounds different, but her reasoning is straightforward.Sometimes, a familiar comfort food does not need a bun to hit the spot.

Klay Thompson agreed to join the Miami Heat on August 21, 2026, after a Dallas Mavericks buyout. The 36-year-old five-time All-Star is expected to sign a two-year, nearly $13 million contract with a player option in Year 2. Thompson averaged 11.7 points and shot 38.3% from three in 2025-26. He now joins Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in Miami.For Miami, the move is about more than adding another veteran name. The Heat have built a frontcourt around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, two players who can command defensive attention near the basket. Thompson gives that lineup a proven perimeter threat who can operate without dominating the ball.Klay Thompson and Dallas agreed to a buyout on August 21, ending his two-year run with the Mavericks. He was owed $17.5 million for 2026-27, but the 36-year-old wanted an opportunity to play for a contender. ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Thompson would head to Miami after clearing waivers.The numbers explain why Miami wanted him. Thompson averaged 11.7 points last season while shooting 38.3% from three. Across his two seasons in Dallas, he averaged 12.9 points and shot 38.7% from deep. He has also been fourth on the NBA's all-time three-point list, with 2,899 made entering this move.The Heat are expected to give Thompson a two-year contract worth nearly $13 million, with a player option for the second season. It represents a major reduction from the $17.5 million salary he was scheduled to receive from Dallas next season.The structure also gives Thompson another chance to control his future after an uneven Dallas tenure. Miami, meanwhile, gets an experienced shooter without committing to a long-term deal.Thompson's fit starts with spacing. Giannis and Adebayo can create pressure inside, while Thompson can punish defenses that collapse toward the paint. Miami also has Andrew Wiggins and Tim Hardaway Jr., adding more veteran wing depth around its new core.There is a clear defensive tradeoff. Thompson is no longer the perimeter stopper he was during Golden State's championship years, and his athleticism has declined after major injuries. Miami will need its interior defense, led by Giannis and Adebayo, to absorb some of that burden.The immediate challenge is making the pieces function together. Thompson has already accepted a reduced role in Dallas, starting only eight of 69 games last season. In Miami, his value may depend less on his scoring volume than on how consistently his shooting creates room for the Heat's two stars.Thompson's Miami chapter now begins with a clear assignment: space the floor, embrace his role and help Giannis and Adebayo push the Heat toward another championship run.
Article Summary: Klay thompson agreed to join the miami heat on august 21, 2026, after a dallas mavericks buyout. The 36-year-old five-time all-star is expected to sign a two-year, nearly $13 million contract with a player option in year 2. He now joins giannis antetokounmpo and bam adebayo in miami.

Article Title: How Aaron Rodgers' decision not to face his old Jets team in preseason speaks volumes about his mindset
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers (Getty Images)

Why did Aaron Rodgers not play against the Jets in preseason 2026?

What does Aaron Rodgers sitting out mean for his final season with the Steelers?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aaron Rodgers sat out Pittsburgh's preseason game against the New York Jets on Friday night, and the Jets made the absence count. The Steelers' offense was shut out in an ugly loss, with the Jets winning 17-0 at Acrisure Stadium. Head coach Mike McCarthy had chosen to rest both veteran quarterbacks, starting Will Howard and giving Drew Allar the second half -- a decision that, given the opponent, carries more than just roster implications. This game was arguably the last time these two teams could meet before Rodgers hangs up his cleats, given no regular-season matchup is scheduled between Pittsburgh and New York this year.The official answer is clean enough. McCarthy wanted to maximize opportunities for his two young quarterbacks. “They’re young,” McCarthy said Wednesday in explaining his decision to play [Will] Howard and [Drew] Allar over the veterans via ESPN’s Brooke Pryor. “Will didn’t get to play last year. … I have some veterans I feel really good about, obviously with Aaron and Mason. I saw what I needed to see from Mason last week. I’ve talked highly about Mason really since the spring. So I really want to max out the opportunities with both Will and Drew.We’ve got two games here, and I want to see those guys play as much as possible, and we’ll continue as we have all camp.”On the field, neither young quarterback delivered. Howard threw two interceptions in the first half and his night ended with the Steelers trailing 7-0. Allar took over for the entire second half but couldn't put points on the board either, with the Jets extending their lead to 17-0 before the final whistle. Cam Johnston's punting was, as one outlet noted, the highlight of the evening -- which says everything about how the offense performed.The scoreline stings, but the context is what makes it interesting. The first big move Aaron Glenn made as Jets head coach was throwing Rodgers out the door. The four-time NFL MVP admitted he felt "disrespected" by that final meeting with Glenn. Rodgers described being blindsided by what he expected to be a real conversation: "That was an interesting two years, to say the least, but I figured that when I flew across the country on my own dime, that there was going to be a conversation. And the confusing thing to me and the strange thing was when I went out there I meet with the coach… we start talking, he runs out of the room."After two forgettable years in New York, Rodgers had an up-and-down first campaign in Pittsburgh, throwing for 3,322 yards with 24 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He came back for one more run specifically because McCarthy, his longtime Green Bay coach, was hired to lead the Steelers. "Yes. This is it," Rodgers told reporters when asked if 2026 would be his final NFL season. There is, by his own admission, zero ambiguity about what this season represents.So what does it mean that he sat out the one preseason game that doubled as a potential final chapter with the Jets? Practically, nothing -- McCarthy made the call, and Rodgers has always treated preseason as time to protect his body. Entering his 22nd season, Rodgers has long been anti-preseason.But symbolically, it fits the broader narrative of a quarterback who has moved past New York entirely. He did not need a staged reunion, a dramatic sideline glance at Aaron Glenn, or a two-minute cameo for closure. The 2026 season is a reunion with McCarthy, who spent 13 years coaching Rodgers in Green Bay before his departure for two fruitless years in New York. That story arc matters far more to Rodgers than anything the Jets could offer now.The Jets won Friday night. Rodgers wasn't watching from the sideline. That, in itself, says plenty.
Article Summary: Aaron rodgers sat out pittsburgh's preseason game against the new york jets. The steelers' offense was shut out in an ugly loss, with the jets winning 17-0 at acrisure stadium. This game was arguably the last time these two teams could meet before rodgers hangs up his cleats.

Mumbai: Prabath Jayasuriya is a rarity in modern-day cricket, especially in the subcontinent, where if you are aged 30 and above, you are not favoured to play international cricket. He waited in the shadows of Sri Lanka’s rich spin tradition. When his chance finally arrived in July 2022, the left-arm spinner grabbed it spectacularly, claiming 12 wickets on Test debut against Australia in Galle.Since then, Jayasuriya has carried Sri Lanka’s spin legacy with distinction, taking 132 wickets in 24 Tests. Ahead of the second Test against India at the SSC, the 34-year-old spoke to TOI about his journey, Sri Lanka’s chances of levelling the series, and why he believes India’s young left-arm spinner Manav Suthar can become one of the world’s best. Excerpts...I had waited a long time for that opportunity. I made my debut after turning 30 and it was a dream start. It remains my favourite match in cricket. After that performance, I realised there was a bigger responsibility because I was representing Sri Lanka. Expectations increased and sometimes the team looks to you for something extra.That brings extra pressure.We knew the pitch would be good for batting early on. KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal used those conditions very well and built the foundation for India. We improved in the second innings but by then the game had gone away from us. India’s batters handled spin well.India batted really well. As a bowling unit, we need to have clearer plans and also execute them better. If we can do that consistently, I believe we can get a better result in the second Test.Joe Root, Kane Williamson and Steve Smith.As players, we have to believe. We have some challenging series coming up, including away tours of Pakistan and New Zealand and a home series against South Africa. The important thing is to stay focused on our processes.Both Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal are out...It’s a big loss. Both are experienced players and important members of the team. At the same time, it opens the door for younger players to step in and prove themselves.He has the potential to become one of the best bowlers in the world. He needs to stay committed to the process, work hard and make sacrifices. If he remains consistent, I believe he can achieve great things.The pitch generally starts turning after the first couple of days. Consistency is the key there. If you keep bowling the right line and length, you can be successful. That’s exactly what Manav did in the first Test.The SSC is my home ground because I play my domestic cricket there. I understand the conditions well. The key is to adapt quickly and keep things simple.Every Test batter is a challenge. Devdutt Padikkal played extremely well in Galle and handled both spin and pace impressively. As the lead spinner in the team, I have a big responsibility. Against strong teams, we need detailed plans and extra effort.
Article Summary: Prabath jayasuriya took 12 wickets on test debut against australia in galle. The 34-year-old believes india's young left-arm spinner manav suthar can become one of the world’s best. Sri lanka lost the first test against india at the ssc by seven wickets.

The Montreal Canadiens are set to honor former goalie Carey Price with a special ceremony at the Bell Center in November. The acknowledgment comes as Price is inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame Class of 2026, another feather in the cap of an incredible career with the historic franchise.Price is one of the most accomplished goalies in Montreal Canadiens history. His upcoming honor also gives fans a new opportunity to honor his legacy while restarting conversations about whether his No. 31 should someday be retired.Carey Price is being honored with induction into the Montreal Canadiens’ Ring of Honor as a tribute to his storied career and contributions to the organization.The ceremony is scheduled for Nov. 10 before the Montreal Canadiens’ game against theMinnesota Wild at Bell Center. Price will be the first former Canadiens player to receive this honor since Shea Weber, joining the most celebrated figures in franchise history.Price was selected fifth overall in the 2005 NHL Draft and spent his entire NHL career with the Montreal Canadiens. He would become the winningest goaltender in franchise history with 361 wins and would go on to be one of the defining players of the modern era.Price’s importance to the Montreal Canadiens went far beyond his numbers. He was the bedrock of the club's goaltending for over a decade and often carried a heavy load in the franchise's most important stretches of competitiveness.His individual awards include the Hart Memorial Trophy, Vezina Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award. In 2015, he also shared the William M. Jennings Trophy, and later won the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy in 2022.Price also added to his legacy on the international stage, helping Team Canada win gold at the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi, adding an Olympic championship to his resume.Carey Price will receive his formal accolades Nov. 10 when the Montreal Canadiens host the Minnesota Wild at the Bell Center.The timing is such that we get to celebrate Price in front of a home crowd while acknowledging his enduring impact on the franchise, GM Mike Montgomery said. The ceremony also comes at a pivotal time in his post-playing career, as his Hockey Hall of Fame induction is scheduled for 2026.Price’s induction into the Ring of Honor has also sparked some debate among Canadiens fans about his No. 31. Some fans believe the number should one day be retired and displayed in the rafters of the Bell Center alongside other legendary Canadiens jerseys.For now, the Ring of Honor induction is yet another great tribute to Price’s legacy. The ceremony is a chance for the Canadiens to officially honor one of the franchise’s greatest netminders with his franchise record 361 wins, major individual awards and Olympic success.
Article Summary: The montreal canadiens are set to honor former goalie carey price with a special ceremony at the bell center in november. The acknowledgment comes as price is inducted into the hockey hall of fame class of 2026. Price will be the first former canadiens player to receive this honor since shea weber.

Tributes pour in for Cedric Sbirrazzuoli following his death

Cedric Sbirrazzuoli, the Monegasque GT and endurance racing driver, has died at the age of 39 after a battle with cancer. He passed away on Thursday, August 20, which was also his 39th birthday.Sbirrazzuoli leaves behind his wife Martina, whom he married only last June. His death has led to tributes from teams, teammates and fellow drivers across the motorsport world. Sbirrazzuoli built a varied career across GT and endurance racing. He competed in several major championships and drove Ferrari machinery for AF Corse and Conquest Racing.Born in Monaco in 1987, CedricSbirrazzuoli began his racing career in the mid-2000s. He started in single-seaters before moving into closed-wheel racing.His career later included competition in GT4, GT2 and the Porsche Carrera Cup. He also raced in several one-make championships. These included the Maserati Trophy and Lamborghini Super Trofeo.A major step in his career came through his connection with AF Corse. The relationship opened the door to Ferrari’s GT racing programme.Sbirrazzuoli went on to race Ferrari’s 458 Italia GT3, 488 and, more recently, the 296 GT3.He competed in a number of important endurance and GT championships.His racing experience included the European Le Mans Series and Asian Le Mans Series. He also competed in GT World Challenge Europe and America. He raced in the Italian GT Championship before moving into IMSA competition.In 2024, Sbirrazzuoli joined Conquest Racing for the IMSA Endurance Cup. He shared the #34 Ferrari with regular drivers Albert Costa and Manny Franco.The season produced some memorable results. The team secured podium finishes at the 24 Hours of Daytona and Watkins Glen. It then ended the campaign with victory at Petit Le Mans.That win became one of the final major highlights of Sbirrazzuoli’s racing career.AF Corse paid tribute to Cedric Sbirrazzuoli after news of his death.“You were a highly talented, determined and professional driver, with the passion and the will to win that are unique to those who truly love racing. But you were also so much more: a genuine, respectful and cheerful person, capable of bringing wholesome enthusiasm and your own special way of living out your passion for motorsport,” recalled AF Corse following the news of his death.“It was a privilege to work and dream together. Your race came to an end far too soon. Your memory will continue to race on forever. We send our warmest thoughts to your wife, your parents and all your loved ones.Farewell, Cedric. Rest in peace”, the statement read.His former teammates also remembered him with great emotion.Michelle Gatting, an Iron Dames racer, shared a tribute while also remembering Luca Persiani, who died in a tragic accident last year.Costa, who raced alongside Sbirrazzuoli at Conquest Racing, also paid tribute to his friend and teammate.Sbirrazzuoli’s career ended far too soon. But his achievements, especially his Petit Le Mans victory, and the memories he created with his teammates will remain part of his racing legacy.

Why this warm-up discourse hits different for Stroud specifically

CJ Stroud spent Thursday night's Texans-Raiders preseason game doing something that looked less like NFL prep and more like a sobriety test gone wrong. Cameras caught him standing on the sideline, thumbs up, eyes darting side to side and up and down without moving his head an inch. Naturally, the internet did what it does best: mocked first, asked questions later. Within hours, the clip was everywhere, with fans comparing him to a man trying to mount a TV or remember which hand he even throws with. Then a doctor showed up in the replies and ended the whole conversation.The clip is genuinely funny out of context. Stroud stuck both thumbs out and tracked them with only his eyes, first horizontally then vertically, totally deadpan, right before leading a touchdown drive.Fans piled on immediately; one joked, "Bro trynna remember which hand he throws with," and another said he looked like he was doing "a field sobriety test." Polymarket Football summed up the vibe best, captioning their post that StroudExcept it wasn't random at all. A doctor jumped into the thread and explained Stroud was doing "saccades," a real vestibular and ocular-motor exercise used in concussion assessments, rehab, and training to sharpen how fast your brain processes visual targets.Translation: while the internet was busy roasting him, Stroud was literally training his brain to read the field faster. This is the kind of viral moment where mockery turns into an unintentional PR win the second someone with a medical degree shows up. Nobody's laughing at "aura points" once you realize the guy was doing legitimate cognitive training on a national broadcast.Context matters here. Stroud is coming off a rough 2025 season where he was ranked 15th among starting quarterbacks, and the Texans got bounced in the divisional round again. So there's already an "is he cooked" undertone following him into this season, and a goofy warm-up clip landing during that exact narrative window made it an easy target.But honestly, the backstory works in his favor. His trainer has previously explained that Stroud's whole pregame routine like basketball throws, towel drills, all of it is built around syncing his body for NFL-speed, quick-release passing rather than big, stretchy warm-up throws. This isn't a guy winging it. This is a quarterback who's clearly doing the unsexy, detail-obsessed work that doesn't show up on a stat sheet, even if it makes for a great meme in the moment.

Article Title: Joe Root creates history in Headingly against Pakistan, moves past Steve Smith in Test cricket
Article Text:
Joe Root creates history

Most catches as a fielder in Test cricket

England leads in Headingly

Joe Root has etched his name into the Test cricket record books, overtaking Australia great Steve Smith to become the leading fielder for most catches in the history of the format. Root reached the landmark during Pakistan's second innings of the first Test against England at Headingley on Friday, taking a sharp catch at leg slip to dismiss Azan Awais off Jofra Archer.The dismissal was the result of a well-executed plan between Root and Archer. Just a couple of deliveries earlier, Root had spoken to Archer and added a leg slip and short leg to the field. Archer then bowled a delivery that jagged sharply into Awais, who attempted to glance it towards fine leg but instead found the inside half of the bat, with Root completing the catch at leg slip.Awais departed for 9 off 14 balls, leaving both Pakistan openers back in the pavilion. The catch was Root's 219th in Test cricket, moving him one clear of Smith, who had 218 catches. Root had equalled Smith's tally during Pakistan's first innings and then moved ahead in the second innings.219 – Joe Root*218 – Steve Smith210 – Rahul Dravid205 – Mahela Jayawardene200 – Jacques KallisRoot's latest milestone came as England continued to dominate the opening Test.England were bowled out for 409 around 40 minutes into the third day's play, having resumed at 366/8. The hosts added 43 runs to their overnight total, with Jofra Archer contributing a valuable 23 before running out of partners. Archer's innings included two fours and a six.Khurram Shahzad claimed the final two England wickets, dismissing Jamie Smith for 25 and bowling Josh Tongue for 8. Despite taking three wickets, Shahzad finished with expensive figures of 3/133. England's first-innings total gave them a commanding 238-run lead after Pakistan had been dismissed for 171 in less than two sessions on the opening day.
Article Summary: Joe root overtakes steve smith to become the leading fielder in test cricket. Root reached the landmark during pakistan's second innings of the first test against england at headingley. England were bowled out for 409 around 40 minutes into the third day's play, having resumed at 366/8.

Article Title: “I don’t hate myself”: Why Kylie Kelce refuses to make Jason Kelce her workout partner despite their decade-long marriage

Kylie Kelce and Jason Kelce have spent years doing life together, from raising four daughters to navigating Jason’s NFL retirement. But there is one part of their routine Kylie would rather keep separate: working out. Her latest comments make it clear that the former Philadelphia Eagles center may be the last person she wants beside her during a gym session.Recently, Kylie joined Olympic rugby medalist Ilona Maher for Power Hour where the conversation quickly turned to Jason. When Maher asked if the couple ever worked out together, Kylie delivered a brutally honest answer that says plenty about their very different approaches to fitness.In a trailer for Ilona Maher’s Power Hour, Maher asked Kylie if she had ever worked out with Jason. However, Kylie did not hesitate.“God, no. I don’t hate myself that much,” Kylie said in the “Power Hour” trailer after Maher asked about exercising with Jason.It was funny, but Kylie had a real reason behind the joke. The couple have lifted together a few times, yet Jason’s approach can make things more complicated for her.The former Philadelphia Eagles center spent 13 seasons training at the highest level of football, so he pays close attention to form and technique.Kylie learned that firsthand during one workout at home.She recalled trying a Romanian deadlift while Jason watched. Instead of simply letting her finish, she asked him to critique her form. Jason’s response was hardly the coaching session she expected.“After a minute of me doing it, I was like, ‘Critique my form,’” Kylie recalled. Jason told her he was “really distracted,” prompting Kylie to call him “useless.”That exchange also explains why Kylie’s latest comments are more than just a marriage joke. She has previously admitted that Jason is extremely particular about technique.During a 2024 interview with “Elite Daily”, Kylie explained that she and Jason had lifted together a few times but rarely found the time to exercise at the same moment. Their schedules often force them to split responsibilities at home. If one person works out, the other usually stays with the children.Kylie also made it clear that she does not necessarily want that arrangement to change. Jason’s training style is another reason. Kylie described him as “such a stickler about technique” and admitted she was not sure she wanted regular criticism from someone who spent many years lifting professionally.The irony is that Kylie Kelce still wants Jason to keep exercising. After Jason Kelce retired from the Eagles, he spoke about his new routine during an appearance on Green Light with Chris Long. He said Kylie wanted him to work out at least three times a week.“She just implemented this,” Jason said on the podcast. “But she said I have to work out a minimum of three days a week. Otherwise, she doesn’t want to deal with me.”Jason also explained why exercise matters to him beyond staying in shape. He said he feels happier, more productive and better with his family after working out.Kylie has her own fitness preferences. She told Elite Daily that she enjoys Peloton workouts, walking, Pilates and yoga. She also likes structured classes because they remind her of her days as an athlete, when coaches told her exactly what to do.So, the Kelces may share almost everything at home, but the gym is clearly different. Kylie wants her workouts to fit her style. Jason wants to focus on technique. And judging by her latest confession, keeping some distance may be exactly what keeps their workouts, and their marriage, fun.

His role as Drax in the Marvel Cinematic Universe helped him become a global movie star.Bautista began training for wrestling in 1999. He eventually signed with WWE and initially competed in Ohio Valley Wrestling under the name Leviathan. He later moved to WWE’s main roster as Deacon Batista.As of 2026, Dave Bautista’s net worth is estimated at around $16 million (per celebrity net worth). His wealth has come from WWE, acting, film projects, endorsements and other business ventures. While wrestling gave him his first major fame, Hollywood has become an important part of his career and earnings.Dave Bautista was born David Michael Bautista Jr. on January 18, 1969, in Washington, D.C. He grew up facing financial difficulties and later worked several jobs before finding his path in bodybuilding and professional wrestling.His career changed after he joined Evolution with Triple H, Ric Flair and Randy Orton . The group became one of WWE’s most successful factions. Bautista later turned against Triple H and won the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 21 in 2005.His championship run lasted 282 days. This helped establish him as one of WWE’s biggest stars. He also gained popularity for winning the Royal Rumble twice in 2005 and 2014. He also earned significant money from wrestling appearances, pay-per-view events and merchandise.Bautista briefly moved into mixed martial arts in 2012. He competed in his only professional MMA fight against Vince Lucero and won by first-round TKO.Acting eventually became the biggest part of his career. Bautista appeared in films and television shows before landing his breakthrough role as Drax the Destroyer in Guardians of the Galaxy in 2014.The Marvel role transformed his career. He returned as Drax in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. These films became major box-office successes and increased his profile around the world.Bautista also appeared in Spectre, Blade Runner 2049 and Dune. His performance in Blade Runner 2049 was particularly praised and showed that he could handle serious dramatic roles.Unlike many former wrestlers, Bautista has continued moving toward demanding acting projects. He has taken roles across action, science fiction and drama. He has been announced as the next lead actor for the God of War TV show.His salary has varied greatly depending on the project. There is no confirmed public figure for his current annual salary. However, major Hollywood roles have become an important source of his income.With his wrestling career, movie earnings and other ventures combined, Bautista’s estimated net worth in 2026 stands at around $16 million. His financial success reflects his transformation from a WWE superstar into one of Hollywood’s most recognisable former professional wrestlers.
